input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# Eliminate non-validated crypto in KServe serving-stack images

## Description

Remediate the KServe serving-stack images so that, on FIPS-enabled OpenShift
clusters, the model serving request path uses only validated cryptographic
modules. This epic covers the audit of cryptographic-library linkage across the
KServe images, the replacement of non-validated crypto usage in the request
path, and the verification that models served through the stack work correctly
under FIPS mode.

## Scope

- Enumerate every KServe image shipped as part of the model serving stack.
- Audit each image's linked cryptographic libraries and identify all
  non-validated crypto usage in the serving request path.
- Replace the identified non-validated crypto usages with validated crypto
  modules and rebuild the affected images.
- Re-audit the rebuilt images to confirm no non-validated crypto remains in the
  request path.
- Validate that model serving (InferenceService request handling) works
  correctly on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster in the deployment modes the
  stack supports.
- Keep all image builds green in the existing build pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A documented crypto-module inventory exists for every KServe image in the
  serving stack, and every non-validated usage in the request path is
  identified. (pass/fail: inventory exists and is complete for all enumerated
  images)
- A re-audit of the rebuilt images shows zero non-validated crypto usage in the
  serving request path.
- InferenceServices serve inference requests correctly on a FIPS-enabled
  OpenShift cluster, verified by functional tests against served models.
- All rebuilt KServe images pass their builds in the existing build pipeline.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled
  clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the
  request path) — this epic delivers that requirement for the KServe images.

## Risks / Notes

- The number of affected images and linkage sites is established by the audit;
  the strategy estimates "several images". If the audit finds materially more,
  re-split this epic along image or sub-system lines (see the decomposition
  summary's re-split trigger).

# Eliminate non-validated crypto in Platform Operator images

## Description

Remediate the Platform Operator images so that the operator itself contains no
non-validated cryptographic modules in its control/request path, and so that it
deploys the model serving stack correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters.
This covers the operator's own image audit and remediation; the serving-stack
workload images are handled by the KServe remediation effort.

## Scope

- Audit the Platform Operator images' linked cryptographic libraries and
  identify all non-validated crypto usage.
- Replace the identified non-validated crypto usages with validated crypto
  modules and rebuild the affected images.
- Re-audit the rebuilt images to confirm no non-validated crypto remains.
- Validate that the operator installs and manages the model serving stack
  successfully on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster.
- Keep all image builds green in the existing build pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A documented crypto-module inventory exists for every Platform Operator
  image, and every non-validated usage is identified.
- A re-audit of the rebuilt images shows zero non-validated crypto usage in the
  operator's control/request path.
- The operator deploys and manages the model serving stack successfully on a
  FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster, verified by functional tests.
- All rebuilt Platform Operator images pass their builds in the existing build
  pipeline.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled
  clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the
  request path) — this epic delivers that requirement for the Platform Operator
  images and for stack deployment under FIPS.

## Risks / Notes

- The strategy lists Platform Operator as an affected component but does not
  describe what changes; the scope above is the minimal functional reading
  (operator images free of non-validated crypto, stack deployable on FIPS
  clusters). Confirm with the strategy author.
- The Platform Operator has no architecture-context file; treat its build and
  onboarding status as unverified until one is added.

# CI gating check for FIPS crypto regressions in serving-stack builds

## Description

Add a gating CI check that fails any model-serving-stack image build which
reintroduces non-validated crypto usage, so that FIPS compliance cannot regress
once the remediated images ship. The check is developed in parallel with the
image remediation work; its coupling to that work is expressed through
acceptance criteria, not through a scheduling dependency.

## Scope

- Implement detection of non-validated crypto-library linkage in
  serving-stack image builds (the detection rules align with the
  validated-module inventory established by the serving-stack image audit).
- Wire the check into the CI build pipelines owned by this epic's team so it
  runs on every KServe serving-stack image build.
- Make the check gating: a build that fails it cannot merge/ship.
- Provide a negative test fixture (a build that links a known non-validated
  crypto library) to prove the check fires, and a clean build to prove it
  passes.
- Time the activation of the gating behavior so it does not fail builds that
  predate the remediated images (advisory first, gating once remediation
  lands).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The check runs automatically on every KServe serving-stack image build in
  CI pipelines owned by RHOAI Serving.
- A build that links non-validated crypto in the request path fails the check,
  demonstrated by the negative test fixture.
- A build using only validated crypto modules passes the check.
- The check is gating, not advisory, at activation time.
- The check's detection rules cover every class of non-validated crypto usage
  identified by the serving-stack image audit (this criterion, not a DAG edge,
  is what couples the check to the remediation's findings).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: CI enforces FIPS regressions — a gating check fails any
  serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.

## Risks / Notes

- HLR-3's "any serving-stack build" spans build pipelines owned by more than
  one team. This epic delivers the gate for the KServe serving-stack image
  builds in the CI pipelines owned by RHOAI Serving. Wiring the same check
  into the Platform Operator build pipeline is coordinated work with RHOAI
  Platform Operators, who own that pipeline and the operator images — it is
  not a deliverable of this epic, and no dependency on their work is implied.
  Track that wiring as a cross-team follow-up when scheduling.

# FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and submission

## Description

Assemble the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model serving
stack — the crypto-module inventory, build attestations, and test results —
and submit it through the mandatory security review board to the external
accredited certification lab. This epic's engineering deliverable ends at a
complete package submitted to the lab; the lab's triage and review timeline,
and the certification decision, are outside its control.

## Scope

- Aggregate the per-image crypto-module inventories produced by the serving
  stack's FIPS remediation into a single module inventory covering every
  in-scope serving-stack image.
- Collect the build attestations produced by the serving-stack build pipelines
  for every remediated image (included as content of the package; no pipeline
  scheduling dependency is implied).
- Collect the test results demonstrating correct operation on FIPS-enabled
  OpenShift clusters with validated crypto modules.
- Assemble the package in the form required by the security review board and
  the certification lab's submission requirements.
- Drive the package through security review board sign-off and submit it to
  the external certification lab.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains a module inventory covering every in-scope
  serving-stack image, with validated/non-validated status per module.
- The evidence package includes the build attestations produced by the build
  pipelines for every remediated serving-stack image.
- The evidence package includes the FIPS-cluster test results for every
  remediated serving-stack image.
- The evidence package is submitted through the security review board to the
  external certification lab.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build
  attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security
    review board to the external certification lab.

## Risks / Notes

- The accredited lab's historical turnaround is six to nine months, and the
  security review board signs off at defined milestones on its own cadence.
  Both are externally controlled schedule constraints that engineering effort
  cannot compress; they are recorded here as risks, not as acceptance
  criteria. The certification grant itself is likewise outside this epic's
  deliverable.
- The lab's triage and acknowledgment of the submission is an outcome
  controlled by the external certification lab and lies beyond HLR-2, which
  ends at submission through the security review board. It is therefore not an
  acceptance criterion; track triage/acknowledgment confirmation as a
  follow-up rather than gating this epic's completion on it.

# Document the serving-stack FIPS support posture

## Description

Author user-facing documentation stating the FIPS support posture of the model
serving stack and the cluster prerequisites for running it on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters. This is substantive content authoring in the Red Hat docs
content process, produced after the implementation work so the documentation
describes what was actually built.

## Scope

Content outline (topics to author or rewrite as new doc topics):

- **FIPS support posture for the model serving stack** — what is supported
  (validated crypto modules in the serving request path), which images are
  covered, and what the posture means for users in regulated environments.
- **Cluster prerequisites** — FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster requirements and
  any configuration users must be aware of before relying on the serving
  stack's FIPS posture.
- **Verification guidance** — how a user or support engineer can confirm the
  deployed serving stack is using validated crypto modules, aligned with the
  shipped evidence and the CI regression gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model serving
  stack and the cluster prerequisites (HLR-4's substance).
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior of the
  remediated serving stack — reviewed by engineers who worked on the FIPS
  remediation, validation, and evidence effort, so no statement contradicts
  what was built or submitted.
- Documentation topics cover every item in the Scope outline above.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster
  prerequisites.

| E003 ∥ E004 (no edge) | Rule 14 | Independent deliverables; HLR-2's package does not include CI-enforcement evidence. |
